pulls.title: 8397997: AArch64: Emit one instruction for masked widening with a non-negative immediate
pulls.author: albertnetymk
pulls.body_excerpt: `ubfizIConvI2LAndI` folded the widening into one `ubfiz`, but only for `2^n - 1` masks (n <= 30) on a plain int. The proposed `convI2L_andI_reg_imm` lifts both restrictions: `iRegI` -> `iRegIorL2I` lets a `ConvL2I` source match, and `immI_bitmask` -> `immILogNonNeg` accepts any 32-bit logical immediate with bit 31 clear. Both relaxation rely on the mask leaving the sign bit clear, so `ubfiz` becomes `andw`, which covers every such mask and zero-extends as a side effect. pulls.title: 8328184: SunMSCAPI ignores LOCALMACHINE when storing and removing certificates
pulls.author: PeyaPeyaPeyang
pulls.body_excerpt: Please review this fix for SunMSCAPI storing and removing certs in `CURRENTUSER` even when a `LOCALMACHINE` keystore is selected. The native `storeCertificate` and `removeCertificate` methods currently use `CertOpenSystemStore`, which opens the `CURRENTUSER` store. This fix passes the store location through JNI and uses `CertOpenStore` with `CERT_SYSTEM_STORE_LOCAL_MACHINE` for `LOCALMACHINE` keystores. pulls.title: 8394577: VectorAPI: Serviceability agent is missing type support for Location::vector
pulls.author: dev-jonghoonpark
pulls.body_excerpt: When C2 scalar-replaces a Vector API object, its payload is recorded in debug info as a `Location::vector`. SA's `Location.getType()` does not recognize this type and throws "should not reach here" when it decodes such a location. The cause is that `vmStructs` does not export HotSpot's `Location::vector`, and SA's `Location` has no corresponding type. ## Changes - `vmStructs.cpp`: export `Location::vector` - SA `Location.java`: add `Type.VECTOR` and handle it in `getType()`, `Type.getValue()` and `printOn()` - `HTMLGenerator.java`: handle `VECTOR` in `locationAsString()` ## Testing - New test

pulls.title: 8394915: Thread dump improvements
pulls.author: AlanBateman
pulls.body_excerpt: This is an update to the thread dump generated by HotSportDiagnosticMXBean.dumpThreads and the jcmd equivalent. 1. The thread output is updated to include the identity string of the Thread object to make it easier link a Thread.join usage to the target thread. 2. The parkBlocker is now set when parked in StructuredTaskScope.join parks to make it easier to find the STS in the thread dump. 3. The thread CPU time is now included for platform threads when available. 4. The JSON dump escapes forward slash between the module and class name in the stack traces. pulls.title: 8395991: Enable pointer authentication in JIT-ed code on Windows/ARM64
pulls.author: raneashay
pulls.body_excerpt: This patch enables PAC and AUT instructions for pointer signing and authentication in JIT code on Windows/ARM64 when "UseBranchProtection" flag is set and when the processor supports the feature. Specifically, JVM detects hardware support by reading ID_AA64ISAR1_EL1 and ID_AA64ISAR2_EL1 registers via CP4031 and CP4032 keys in the Windows registry. Then, if the "UseBranchProtection" flag is set, then HotSpot emits the signing and authenticating instructions. pulls.title: 8390049: Zero-copy vector alternative to a scalar loop over charAt
pulls.author: cushon
pulls.body_excerpt: This change adds Vector API methods that load the code units of a `java.lang.String` into a vector without copying, to allow processing a `String` with a vector loop instead of a scalar loop over `charAt`. As discussed in the [panama-dev@ thread 'String processing and Vector APIs'](https://mail.openjdk.org/archives/list/panama-dev@openjdk.org/thread/YSPX3TBXZTZEFZNXWDYOZCWLUQPC62P6/), one motivating use-case is a regex library that wants to accelerate scans for character classes. Implementing these methods outside the JDK using scalar `charAt` loops is slower than a vectorized implementation.

pulls.author: ruben-arm
pulls.body_excerpt: Extend MOVK-based scheme to MOVK/MOVZ allowing to store 19 bits of metadata directly. pulls.title: 8342869: Errors related to unused code on Windows after 8339120 in awt
pulls.author: TheShermanTanker
pulls.body_excerpt: After 8339120, gcc began catching many different instances of unused code in the Windows specific codebase. Some of these seem to be bugs. I've taken the effort to mark out all the relevant globals and locals that trigger the unused warnings and addressed all of them by commenting out the code as appropriate. I am confident that in many cases this simplistic approach of commenting out code does not fix the underlying issue, and the warning actually found a bug that should be fixed.
